title: Fail-closed benchmark audits + PolicyArtifact identity
description:
## Why
Evaluation is not trustworthy for published claims. Missing audit fields default to zero (absent RAM-write/load/assist interpreted as no interventions). A backend with no instrumentation can appear Clean. Learned policy identity uses implementation source/bytecode, not model weights.

## Goal
AuditedEnv (or capability-bearing wrapper) + PolicyArtifact manifest so Clean claims and learned policies are fail-closed.

## Work
1. **AuditedEnv / capability probe** — runner must prove RAM writes, state loads, assists are *observable*; otherwise reject Clean / force Unknown intervention class
2. **Default-missing ≠ zero** — benchmark.py must not treat absent instrumentation as clean
3. **PolicyArtifact** — checkpoint SHA/digest, algorithm, hyperparameters, training seed, obs/action/reward schema digests, ROM/state/core identity, dependency lock, source commit
4. Wire claim validator (rr-gbd.31) to reject publication without audit proof + artifact identity for learned policies

## Acceptance
- [ ] Uninstrumented env cannot produce Clean claim
- [ ] Synthetic test: missing audit fields → fail closed (not silent zero)
- [ ] PolicyArtifact round-trip; load rejects weight/schema mismatch
- [ ] At least one game path (MK or SM structured) emits full audit trail in dry-run

## Anchors
- retro_harness/benchmark.py (~434 missing→zero, ~2295 policy identity)
notes: MATURITY 2026-08-09: first real-game consumer through SM-rando Clean vertical audit and learned Landing BC PolicyArtifact. Not publication-ready: rr-gbd.33 campaign runner and a second independent game consumer remain.

title: SolverSession runtime: SkillSpec lifecycle, dispatch, recovery
description:
## Why
Architecture says observe→plan→invoke skill→replan, but there is no shared execution kernel. protocol.py Skill/Protocol is too small with almost no cross-game adoption. rr-gbd.30 covers binding/evidence readiness, not lifecycle or recovery.

## Goal
Shared solver runtime that enforces preconditions, dispatches skills, validates postconditions, classifies failure, updates state, and replans.

## Types
- SkillSpec — typed observation requirements, applicability, expected progression/resource deltas
- SkillInstance — bound policy + config + identity
- SkillOutcome — success | retryable_failure | terminal_failure | timeout; observed deltas; recovery/replan hints
- SolverSession — frame/action lifecycle, plan step, invoke, validate, replan, full trace + policy identity

## Acceptance
- [ ] API + unit tests for lifecycle states
- [ ] Injected failure → classified outcome → successful replan path in fixture
- [ ] Not considered done until multi-edge real vertical slice (child bead) closes
- [ ] protocol.py either absorbed or thin facade; document adoption path

## Out of scope here
Full multi-game edge binding (see vertical slice bead). .30 remains edge binding/evidence only.
close_reason: Implemented typed SkillSpec/SkillInstance/SkillOutcome and SolverSession lifecycle with action frames, pre/post validation, retry/timeout classification, recovery replanning, and policy-identified traces; runtime unit acceptance passes, real consumer remains rr-gbd.38.

title: Versioned env/obs/action/reward/wrapper contracts
description:
## Why
retro_harness/env.py carries only game/path/action size/players. Action tables and feature vectors are handwritten; model compatibility is largely tensor-dimension matching. title: Tiered test and CI gates (core / ML / game / ROM smoke)

## Why
Default checkout cannot collect its configured suite: fighters __init__ eagerly imports optional stable_baselines3 (collection errors). pyproject test paths omit many game test files; no .github CI directory.

## Goal
Establish fail-closed, tiered gates so "green" means something and shared subsystems require real consumers before completion claims.

## Tiers
1. **core** — no ROM, no ML: harness + graph + docs collect/pass always

3. **all-game no-ROM** — every game unit/offline test under snes/*/nes/* that needs no ROM
4. **opt-in real-ROM smoke matrix** — selected M1 boots / continuous dry markers
5. **real-consumer acceptance** — shared subsystem not "complete" until ≥1 real game consumer (scaffold → fake-tested → real-ROM → first consumer → second consumer → publication-ready)

- [ ] pyproject test config includes or explicitly opts out game suites with rationale

**P0 structural.** k4_wave.py is a brand-new 0→1345 line megafile holding three independent room policies. Already caused a silent continuous/pure regression.

## Incident evidence
Commit `9f5b2c6` (rr-dbu.1): K4.9/K4.10 added Double Chamber `_DOOR_X = 920`, which **overwrote** Bubble sill `_DOOR_X = 470` at import time so blue-door push never shot. Fix was prefix rename (`_BSC_DOOR_*` / `_DC_DOOR_*`) — a bandage, not a design.

## Current structure (one file)
| Segment | Role | Approx lines |
|---------|------|--------------|
| Bubble → Single | blue door | ~45–308 |
| Single → Double | missile red door | ~310–575 |
| Double → Wave | gate RLE + Super door + PLM | ~577–1345 |

Also: three near-identical `_escape_kb` / `_escape_kb_sc` / `_escape_kb_dc` (only `stop_room_id` differs); soft-budget `pass` dead code ×3; inlined `_HUMAN_GATE_OPEN_RLE` despite `data/double_chamber_gate_open_rle.json`.

## Why this blocks tip extension
Ice pure (rr-dbu.11) and Moat will either (a) stuff more rooms into k4_wave, re-risking constant shadow, or (b) fork more megafiles. Spazer package already proved the correct multi-hop layout.

## Gold-standard reference
`routes/kpdr/spazer/`:
- geometry.py — named bands + predicates
- scripts.py — RLE tables
- helpers.py — play_script / lag break
- climb / approach / collect / drop / detour — one hop each
- __init__.py — public re-exports

## Target layout
```
routes/kpdr/wave/
  __init__.py              # re-export play_* + WAVE_BEAM_MASK
  geometry.py              # bands, seats, WAVE_BEAM_MASK, predicates
  scripts.py               # load or define RLE (prefer data/*.json — see sibling bead)
  bubble_to_single.py
  single_to_double.py
  double_to_wave.py
  helpers.py               # shared seat settle / one escape helper if not yet global
```
Keep `k4_wave.py` as a **thin re-export facade** (like k4_norfair) so registry / spine_hops / tests importing k4_wave or k4_norfair stay stable.

## Out of scope
- Route knob changes
- STATUS promote
- Implementing Ice
design:
1. Create package skeleton with empty modules + geometry constants moved first (no logic change).
2. Move Bubble→Single helpers + play_* with imports adjusted.
3. Move Single→Double.
4. Move Double→Wave (RLE may stay temporarily if RLE bead not done; do not re-inline).
5. k4_wave.py becomes `from super_metroid.routes.kpdr.wave import *` facade.
6. k4_norfair / registry / spine_hops keep working via existing import paths.
7. Run unit registration tests + dual pure Wave stack if sources exist.

Constant rule after split: geometry names are room-prefixed in geometry.py; never bare `_DOOR_X` at package import root for multi-hop constants.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] No routes/kpdr file for Wave multi-hop exceeds ~500 lines (package pieces)
- [ ] k4_wave.py is thin facade only (or deleted with imports updated)
- [ ] get_segment bubble_to_single / single_to_double / double_chamber_to_wave still resolve
- [ ] test_k4_norfair_scaffold + continuous tip hop ids still pass
- [ ] Dual pure Wave stack still GREEN if run (no intentional behavior change)
- [ ] No module-level constant can shadow another room's door X by import order
close_reason: Packaged k4_wave → routes/kpdr/wave/ (facade 30f); modules ≤403 lines; room-prefixed geometry; tests green

title: Pass A: canonicalize human RLE (promote play_script, load data/*.json)
description:
## Severity
**P0 maintainability / dual source of truth.** Human gate-open sequence exists twice:

1. **Product (used):** inlined `_HUMAN_GATE_OPEN_RLE` tuple inside k4_wave.py (~45 RLE rows, tape f4650–5200)
2. **Data (unused by product):** `routes/kpdr/data/double_chamber_gate_open_rle.json`
3. **Also:** `dc_missile_wave_take04_paths.json` from parse_human_take — practice/docs, not product load

Spazer already has the right pattern buried in the wrong package:
- `routes/kpdr/spazer/scripts.py` — `RleScript` type + FLOOR_MID_RLE etc.
- `routes/kpdr/spazer/helpers.play_script` — only Spazer climb/approach/drop import it

Wave reimplemented the RLE frame loop with mid-hit abort/retry. Next tip (Ice/Moat/WJ) will paste more tuples into Python.

## Failure mode if unfixed
- JSON bitrots while Python is hand-edited (or reverse)
- Probe/practice tools and product controllers diverge
- Agents invent shot cadences because the load path is unclear (docs already say “do not invent shot cadences”)

## Required shape
1. Promote `RleScript` + `play_script` to a shared home:
   - Prefer `routes/controller_common.py` or new `routes/rle.py`
2. Wave double-chamber gate open **loads** `data/double_chamber_gate_open_rle.json` (normalize schema n/b vs tuple)
3. Delete inlined `_HUMAN_GATE_OPEN_RLE` from product code
4. Spazer can keep local scripts.py tables short-term but should import shared play_script (migrate Spazer tables later optional)
5. Reactive wrapper stays room-specific (Kamer seat, hit abort, floor recover, retry ≤3) **around** play_script — do not fork a second RLE player

## Related tools
- `scripts/tools/parse_human_take.py` — path JSON emitter; align RLE field schema with product loader
- `spazer/helpers.play_script` — canonical implementation to lift
design:
Loader sketch:
- `load_rle_json(path) -> RleScript` accepting list of {n, b} or [n, buttons]
- `play_script(session, runs, *, reason, room_id, stop_when=None, on_lag=...)`
- Wave `_dc_open_blue_gate` uses load once (module import or cached) then play_script with stop_when past_gate / room leave; outer retry loop unchanged

Tests:
- unit: load fixture JSON equals known tuple
- registration / pure dual Wave if available still green
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] play_script + RleScript live outside spazer/ (controller_common or routes/rle)
- [ ] Wave gate-open product path loads data/double_chamber_gate_open_rle.json
- [ ] No inlined _HUMAN_GATE_OPEN_RLE (or equivalent paste) in Python controllers
- [ ] Spazer uses shared play_script (not a private duplicate implementation)
- [ ] Dual pure double_chamber_to_wave still opens gate (no intentional cadence change)
close_reason: routes/rle.py play_script+load_rle_json; Wave gate loads data/*.json; Spazer re-exports shared player; test_rle green

title: Library → bank → reactive route script (multi-take mix + AP)
description:
Product architecture for full-run human recording + skill mix + reactive autopilot.

## Layers (do not collapse)
1. **Library of takes** — many recordings (segments/sN, practice series); never overwrite good tapes.
2. **Skill bank (mix)** — hop_key → many candidates; best() prefers dual_green then min frames.
3. **Route script (reactive)** — decisions/recovery/AP handoff; pure/FSM/policy uses bank as options.

## Glossary (authoritative)
- **Hop:** One settled room visit unit: enter pin → leave next room (or end_xy for final hop). Inventory-aware identity via hop_key = room:from→to:items. Unit of dual-green, bank PB, hill-climb, and open-loop body export.
- **Open-loop:** Replay a fixed SNES-12 button body from a live pin without mid-body branching. Safe unit = one hop from entry_anchor. Unsafe = multi-minute mega-tape from boot for pin recovery. Reactive script may *choose* which open-loop skill to run; the body itself is not the decision layer.

## Done when
- Multi-take library + bank ranking usable for mix.
- Natural-entry compose (leave of A accepts as entry of B) dual-green on a spine slice.
- Thin route index: live room+items → skill.
- Mid-run AP toggle only runs dual_green/pure skills; handback predicate works on one hard hop.

See docs/tasks/HUMAN_TAPE_PIPELINE.md and docs/RUN_TIMING_AND_SKILL_BANK.md.

title: Bounded resource- and risk-aware planning (keys/consumables/reliability)
description:
## Why
Planner is intentionally monotonic: capabilities only grow; consumables, keys, and resource counts are excluded (adventure/graph.py ~329). That will block real ALTTP/SM/rando routes (small keys, bombs, missiles, magic, energy, money, time).

## Goal
Bounded typed resources, edge deltas, failure probability, and duration/resource distributions. Planner cost reflects empirical skill reliability, not only a static float.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Resource types + edge consume/produce deltas with bounds
- [ ] PlanResult exposes resource trajectory and blockers
- [ ] Cost model can incorporate SkillOutcome reliability stats
- [ ] Fixture: key-door or missile-door graph requires resource-aware path
- [ ] Defer broad adoption until vertical slice (multi-edge session) demonstrates need

## Explicitly excluded from current planner — this bead tracks the expansion
notes: MATURITY 2026-08-09: fake-tested with key/missile/resource-bound and SkillOutcome reliability golden fixtures. No game-owned resource planner consumer yet.
close_reason: Added deterministic bounded resource-state search with typed bounded consumable/renewable/safety resources, edge consume/produce/minimum profiles, resource trajectories and blockers on PlanResult, and risk-adjusted costs driven by aggregated SkillOutcome reliability/duration. Golden key-door, missile, risk-ranking, and budget tests pass.

title: Canonical Trajectory + counterexample data layer
description:
## Why
RunManifest is a session summary, not an imitation dataset. rr-gbd.17 (imitation → condition-robust skills) is too vague without a versioned trajectory format.

## Goal
Versioned Trajectory format: observation/schema identity, actions, reward components, milestones, terminal reason, state digests, source provenance. Use for BC, DAgger-style corrections, failure clustering, and regression replay.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Trajectory schema + schema digest (align with PolicyArtifact / contracts)
- [ ] Export from SolverSession and/or continuous dry-runs
- [ ] Import path for BC or offline replay of one failure cluster
- [ ] rr-gbd.17 depends on this for any real imitation work
- [ ] Counterexample library: failed attempts retained, not only successes

## Relationship
Complements rr-gbd.17 (consumer) and EntryStateCorpus (state distribution); Trajectory is time-series experience.
notes: MATURITY 2026-08-09: first real-game consumer. SM-rando retains a canonical real vertical trajectory, recovered-failure counterexample, and six held-out BC eval trajectories. No second independent game consumer.
close_reason: Added versioned canonical Trajectory identity with exact SolverSession actions/observation boundaries, reward components, milestones, terminal/state/provenance fields; content-addressed counterexample library and offline cluster import. Re-ran the real vertical slice: 3 replayable macro steps plus the retained injected-failure episode.

title: One BC/RL skill experiment on held-out natural-entry states
description:
## Why
Defer algorithm sweeps until vertical path exists. One focused experiment validates EntryStateCorpus + contracts + Trajectory on a real skill.

## Goal
Train one skill (BC and/or short RL fine-tune) on train-split EntryStateCorpus; evaluate on held-out predecessor states; report train/eval gap with PolicyArtifact + fail-closed audit.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Uses EntryStateCorpus holdout (not single save-state)
- [ ] Emits PolicyArtifact + contract digests
- [ ] Train vs held-out eval metrics published under game docs/recordings
- [ ] No claim of superiority over structured skill unless audited eval wins
- [ ] Explicitly does NOT expand to multi-game PPO farm

## Depends on
Corpus, contracts, preferably Trajectory export, and ideally vertical slice for failure data.
close_reason: Trained a contract-bound linear behavior clone on 58 EntryStateCorpus train states only (0 eval states used): it predicts wait-to-validated-predecessor-handoff then dispatches the unchanged real Landing skill. Real-ROM audited evaluation scored 58/58 train and 6/6 held out versus structured baseline 0/58 and 0/6; six canonical eval trajectories retained. Decision remains candidate-only/not deployed pending new predecessor trajectories.

```
_escape_kb      → stop_room_id=ROOM_SINGLE_CHAMBER
_escape_kb_sc   → stop_room_id=ROOM_DOUBLE_CHAMBER
```

Only stop_room_id differs. Same call shape is also inlined repeatedly in to_speed.py, speed_return.py, k4_cathedral.py, moat.py (escape_knockback_spin with run_frames=6, spin_frames=18).

## Problem B — soft-budget pass is dead ceremony
```
if session.frame - start > _TOTAL_BUDGET:
    pass  # soft budget; room success is the gate
```
Present in all three Wave plays, speed_return, to_speed. Constants that never enforce anything are noise.

## Fix
1. Canonical thin helper (controller_common or skills/knockback):
   escape_kb(session, label, prefer, *, stop_room_id)
2. Room policies pass leave-room id; delete private clones.
3. Soft budgets: hard-fail with TimeoutError OR delete constants entirely (prefer delete if room success is the only gate).

## Couple with
Wave package (rr-7sn.1) so helpers land in wave/helpers or shared layer once, not thrice then moved.

title: Pass B: second-pass consolidate green room policies (shared primitives)
description:
## Severity
P2 consolidation after Pass A. Behavior-preserving; delete concepts, not rename.

## Problem
Every pure hop invents the same shell:
require_room → unmorph/select → phase loops (knockback? band? hold) → wait_ordinary_room → TimeoutError dump

Fine at 3 rooms; toxic at Wave + Ice + Moat + second-pass of Cathedral/Speed/Spazer.

## Priority order (after Pass A lands)
1. Wave package internals — geometry/scripts/helpers; no duplicated phase loops across three plays
2. Spazer — drop private _compat aliases when unused; import shared play_script
3. to_speed + speed_return — share door-band + knockback patterns with Wave helpers
4. k4_cathedral — split if approaching ~800 before next tip
5. Prefer pure functions + shared primitives; **do not** invent a heavy RoomPolicy class hierarchy

## Out of scope
- New knobs / STATUS claims
- Ice pure implementation
design: Depends on Pass A: Wave package (rr-7sn.1), RLE canon (rr-7sn.2), escape_kb (rr-7sn.5) so consolidation reuses shared helpers rather than inventing a fourth copy.
